claims.nodeLabel: FY2026 NDAA, Public Law 119-60 - secs. 1671-1673, NORAD/NORTHCOM intercept briefings and UAP classification-guide accounting
claims.text: Sec. 1672(a) repeals sec. 413 of the IAA for FY2022 (50 U.S.C. 3373a). Sec. 1672(b) rewrites 50 U.S.C. 3373(f)(1)(A) to read: 'The Director of National Intelligence and the Secretary of Defense shall jointly require that each element of the intelligence community and component of the Department of Defense with data relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena makes such data available immediately to the Office in a manner that protects intelligence sources and methods.' The added qualifier 'in a manner that protects intelligence sources and methods' is new and was not in the repealed provision.

claims.nodeLabel: FY2026 NDAA, Public Law 119-60 - secs. 1671-1673, NORAD/NORTHCOM intercept briefings and UAP classification-guide accounting
claims.text: Sec. 1673(a), note '50 USC 3373 note', requires the Director of AARO within 180 days of enactment to 'make an accounting of security classification guides that apply to information used for reports and investigations of unidentified anomalous phenomena' and permits issuance of 'a consolidated security classification matrix for programs relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena to provide a resource for programs that support or may be affected by investigations relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena.' Sec. 1673(b) requires the results to be included in the 2026 annual report under 50 U.S.C. 3373(k).

claims.nodeLabel: FY2026 NDAA, Public Law 119-60 - secs. 1671-1673, NORAD/NORTHCOM intercept briefings and UAP classification-guide accounting
claims.text: Sec. 1671(b), note '50 USC 3373 note', imposes a retrospective look-back: the first briefing after enactment 'shall include details on any unidentified anomalous phenomena intercepts conducted by the North American Aerospace Defense Command or the United States Northern Command not previously provided that occurred during the period beginning on January 1, 2004, and ending on the last day of the period otherwise covered by the briefing.'

claims.nodeLabel: FY2026 NDAA, Public Law 119-60 - secs. 1671-1673, NORAD/NORTHCOM intercept briefings and UAP classification-guide accounting
claims.text: The 1 January 2004 look-back date in sec. 1671(b) is the month of the USS Nimitz / 'Tic Tac' encounters. Congress selected a start date that reaches back to the earliest incident in the modern public record rather than to AARO's creation, indicating the committees believe intercept records from that period exist and have not been briefed. Reasoning: no other event anchors that specific date in UAP legislative history.

claims.nodeLabel: FY2026 NDAA, Public Law 119-60 - secs. 1671-1673, NORAD/NORTHCOM intercept briefings and UAP classification-guide accounting
claims.text: Sec. 1673's premise is that no one currently has a map of which classification guides control UAP information across the government - four years after AARO was created by statute. The authorisation of a 'consolidated security classification matrix' for 'programs relating to unidentified anomalous phenomena' is an admission in enacted law that a plurality of such programs exists and that their classification authorities are not centrally known. Reasoning: Congress does not order an accounting of guides that are already inventoried.

claims.nodeLabel: Line item 'CLASSIFIED PROGRAMS' / Program Element 9999999999
claims.text: The $26.9 billion Other Procurement, Air Force classified line is the principal 'pass-through': it is carried on the Air Force's books and counted against the Air Force topline but is not the Air Force's money to spend. Reasoning: the sum vastly exceeds any plausible Air Force-controlled classified procurement requirement, the account has historically carried national reconnaissance funding, and the Air Force has repeatedly and publicly complained that its published topline overstates its actual resources by roughly this magnitude.

edges.label: DoDI 5205.11 para. 7.2.h - waived-programme justification materials go only to committee staff directors
edges.note: DoDI 5205.11 para. 7.2.h, 'Congressional Budget Justification Materials': 'The DoD will conform to all congressional reporting requirements. The DoD will submit to the congressional defense and intelligence committees such additional materials as are requested by the committees and are within the jurisdiction of each committee. Justification materials for waived programs will be presented only to the committee staff directors.' This is the best available primary evidence that DoD continued to route waived-programme justification material to the defense committees after the 31 December 2021 termination of 10 U.S.C. 119(a) and (b) - but note that it routes that material to staff directors rather than through the 119(e)(2) chair-and-ranking channel, and it rests on committee request rather than on a standing statutory reporting duty.
